chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: How John Collins has changed: staying current with rock work
summary: He likes innovation, plays with young musicians, and has recorded rock beats for Capitol and Motown with wah-wah and synthesizer.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well, I always -- I think young, I think -- I like innovations. So I'm always trying this and I'm always trying this, you know. And -- still sitting in the back of the church hearing things.

Just about, and doing them, you know. I worked with the young musicians, I record rock and roll, I still play the bebop, you know. As I say I'm totally involved in music. Oh, gosh, I've done so many rock beats for Capitol and Motown, you know. Oh, I've done a few with Mr. Page. I said that advisedly. You know, and what's the -- oh, gosh, I don't know who these people are, Pat, you know, I mean I come out of there and with my wawa and my synthesizer and all of this. My -- you know, I have to carry all this equipment, you know.
Well, now, yes, surprisingly yes. You know, I wouldn't make it my life's work, you know, but it's music, it's a lot to be said for it.
